full_judgment:
Sharif Uddin Chaklader J: Having aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 26-11-2000 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Laxmipur in Title Appeal No. 21 of 1997 heard analogously with Title Appeal No. 50 of 1997 allowing the appeals thereby on reversing the judgment and decree dated 21-11-1996 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Additional Court, Laxmipur decreed Title Suit No. 56 of 1991.

2. Defendant Nos. 8 and 9 preferred these two Civil Revision No. 4016 of 2009 and Civil Revision No. 1148 of 2002 and both these revision having arisen from same suit and from same judgment and decree these two revisions are taken up together for disposal and this judgment would govern both these two rules.

3. Plaintiff-opposite party instituted the aforesaid suit praying for decree as:-

"অতএব বাদী প্রার্থনা করেন যে,

(ক) নিম্ন (ক) তপছিল ভূমিতে বাদীর রয়তি স্বত্ব ঘোষনার মর্মে ডিক্রি দেওয়ার মর্জি হয়।"

(খ) নিম্ন (খ) তপছিলে উল্লেখিত লক্ষ্মীপুর সহকারী কমিশনার ভূমি অফিসের ১৯৮৩/৮৪ ইং সনের ১ নং নামজারী ও  জমা খারিজ দরখাস্তে ২৭-৭-৮৩ ইং তারিখে ৪/৫ নং বিবাদীর নমে হোল্ডিং খতিয়ান খোলার আদেশ বেআইনী ও বাতিল ঘোষনার মর্মে ডিক্রি দানের মর্জি হয়। ১০(ম) (১) বাদী নালিশী রায়তিতে শেঃ ১০.৫ ডিং ভূমিতে মালিক ও দখলকার থাকায় উক্ত ভূমি বাবত বাবত বাদীকে পৃথক ছাহামের প্রদানে বন্টনের প্রাথমিক ডিক্রিদানের আজ্ঞা হয়। ১০(ম) (২) আদালতের নির্ধারিত সময়ের মধ্যে শরীফ বিবাদীগন আপোষে বাদীর অংশের ভূমি পৃথকভাবে বন্টন করিয়া না দিলে আদালত বাদী হইতে ক্ষয়াদি গ্রহণে জনৈক সিভিল কোর্ট কমিশনার নিযুক্ত ক্রমে চিটা নকশা ফিল্ড বুক ইত্যাদি প্রস্তুত ক্রমে বন্টনের ফাইনাল ডিক্রি দানের আজ্ঞা হয়।

(গ) সমস্ত আদালত ব্যায় বাদীর অনুকুলে বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে ডিক্রি দেওয়ার মর্জি হয়।

(ঘ) অথবা অবস্থা ও প্রমান দৃষ্টে বাদী অন্য যে ভাবে যে যে প্রতিকার পাইতে পারে তৎমর্মে ডিক্রি দেওয়ার মর্জি হয়।"

4. It is the case of plaintiff that suit land comprising 29 decimals of land of dag No. 3246 of District settlement khatian No. 458 and No. 63 Nancha Nagar Mouzajoma of dag No. 21 originally belonged to Amzad Khalasi. Amzad Khalasi sold 10.5 decimals of land out of 29 decimals of land to Abul Hasim. Joynal Abedin purchased 7.5 decimals, Sabina Khatoon also purchased 4 decimals and 7.5 decimals of land purchased by Bazaler Rahman from Amzad Khalasi. The suit land having been recorded in 63 No. Bancha Nagar Mouza in khatian No. 909 in the name of Abul Hasim 4 annas share in the name of Joynal Abedin 2 annas share, in the name of Sabina Khatoon 4 annas share, 4 ann as share in the name of Bazaler Rahman correctly. In getting settlement, in khatian No. 909, the name of Sabina Khatoon has been wrongly recorded. Sabina Khatoon out of her share, sold 4 decimals of land by saf kabala dated 27th Falgun, 1339 B.S. corresponding to 11-3-1933 to Arafatunnessa. Abul Hasim sold his 6 annas share comprising 10.5 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman, Joynul Abedin in 4 annas share transferred 7.25 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman. In this way, Bazaler Rahman with his 4 annas share, purchased 10 annas share, in total purchased 14 annas share of 25 decimals of land, died leaving 3 sons, defendant No. 1-3. Arafatunnessa having owner of 4 decimals of land died leaving 2 sons, Abdul Aziz Patwari and Abdul Hasim Patwari and daughter, Anwara Begum. Abdul Aziz Patwari purchased 6 decimals of land from Bazaler Rahman by kabala dated 17-4-1944. In this way Abdul Aziz Patwari having owner of 7.5 decimals of land by purchase and by inheritance, died, leaving son, Sherajul Islam, 3 daughters, Parul Begum, Minara Begum, Shamsur Nahar and wife, Fatema Bibi. Fatema Bibi, Sherajul Islam and Shamsur Nahar jointly by saf kabala deed No. 12950 dated 29-11-1990 transferred 3 and 5/8 decimals of land to plaintiff Sherajul Islam and Shamsun Nahar sold 3 and 5/8 decimals of land by registered deed No. 1295 dated 29-11-1990 to plaintiff. At the time of death of Hossain Ahmed, he was survived by son, Shahab Uddin and daughter, Sabina Khatoon. On the death of Anwara Khatoon, her two sons, Shah Alam and Bachu Mea became owner of her property. Shahab Uddin, Shah Alam and Bachu Mea sold 3 decimals of land by baina, which was converted to registered document dated 20-4-1991. In this way plaintiff become owner by purchase and by inheritance of the scheduled land. After purchase, plaintiff went to pay rent to the local Tahsil Office on 15-2-1991 and came to know that out of suit land, during MRR survey, 29 decimals of land recorded in the name of his predecessor of No. 63 Bancha Nagar Mouza, Khatian No. 767, dag No. 8351. For total land of 29 decimals, plaintiff came to know that for aforesaid land in Mutation Case No. 111983-84 of the court of Assistant Commissioner (Revenue) the name of Bazaler Rahman was replaced and was recorded in the name of defendant Nos. 4-5 in holding No. 2405, khatian No.2404 and holding No. 2395 and khatian No. 2396. It is further case of plaintiffs that for the aforesaid wrong recording either in the name of Bazaler Rahman or in the name of defendant Nos. 3-4 or defendant No. 1-5, title, interest and possession of plaintiff has not been effected as the plaintiff purchased the suit land finding title of his predecessor and plaintiff could not know of the aforesaid wrong recording. The aforesaid wrong recording a cloud has been cast upon title of plaintiff which required to be removed, as such, plaintiff instituted the suit. For the cause of action of suit plaintiff has stated as :-

"ঐ অবস্থায় বাদীর মালিকী দখলীয় নিম্ন তপছিল ভূমি ১-৩ নং বিবাদীর মৌরশ বজলের রহমনের নামে এম, আর, আর, জরিপে ভূল রেকর্ড হওয়ায় এবং উক্ত ভূমি বাবৎ ৪/৫ নং বিবাদিগন তাহাদের নামে ভিন্ন খতিয়ান খোলার ঘটনা করায়এবং তাহা এমন প্রকাশ পাওয়ায় নিম্ন তপছিল ভূমিতে বাদীর স্বত্ব দখলের উপর এক মেঘাবরন ঝুকিয়া পড়িয়াছে। উক্তকালিমা দুরীভূত হওয়া একান্ত আবশ্যক। তাই নিম্ন তপছিল ভূমিতে বাদীর রায়তি স্বত্ব ঘোষনার মর্মে অত্রাদালতে অত্র নালিশ দায়ের করিতে বাধ্য হইলেক।

তর্কিত ভ্রমাত্মক খতিয়ানের বিষয় বাদী যথা সময়ে কিছুমাত্র অবগত ছিল না চলিত ১৯৯১ ইং সনের ফ্রেব্রুয়ারী মাসের ১ম দিকে বাদী তহশিল অফিসের খাজনা দিতে গেলে উক্ত ভুল খতিয়ানের বিষয় অবগত হয়। এবং ভূয়া জমা খারিজ ও মানজারী মুলে ৪/৫ নং বিবাদীর নামে ভূয়া খতিয়ান খোলার বিষয়  অবগত হয়। "

5. Plaintiff has described schedule of the property as :-

"(ক) জিলা লক্ষ্মীপুর উপজেলা লক্ষ্মীপুরের অধীনে ৬৩ নং বাঞ্জানগর মৌজার জিলা জরিপী ৪৫৮ নং খতিয়ানভূক্ত ৩২৪৬ দাগে ২৯ শতাংশ ভূমি আন্দরে ১০ শতাংশ ভূমি উক্ত ভূমি পোট জরিপে ৯০৯ নং খতিয়ানভূক্ত ৮৩৫১ দাগে রেকর্ড হয়। যাহা পরবর্তী এম,আর,আর, জরিপে ৬৩ নং বাঞ্জানগর মৌজার ৭৬৭ নং খতিয়ানভূক্ত ৮৩৫১ দাগে রেকর্ড হয় উহাই বিরোধীয় ভূমি হয়।"

(খ)লক্ষ্মীপুর সহকারী কমিশনার ভূমি অফিসের ১৯৮৩/৮৪ ইং সনের ১ নং নামজারী জমা খারিজ দরখাস্তে ২৭-৭-৮৩ ইং তারিখের আদেশে ৪/৫ নং বিবাদীর নামীয় ২৪০৫ নং হোঃ ২৪০৪ নং খতিয়া এবং ২৩৯৫ নং হোল্ডিং ২৩৯৬ নং খতিয়ান বিরোধীয় খতিয়ান হয়।"

6.	The suit has been contested by defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 by a single written statement and also by additional written statement and defendant Nos. 11-12 by single written statement.

7.	The case of defendant Nos. 8,9 and 10 is that suit land consisting of 29 decimals recorded in PS khatian No. 909 and District Survey khatian No. 449 was demarcated as Abul Hasim in 6 anna, Joybul Abedin in 6 anna, Bazaler Rahman in 4 anna and Sabina Khatoon in 2 anna, with joma of Taka 2.25 which has been wrongly recorded in PS survey. JoynalAbedin in 4 annas share got 7.25 decimals of land and as plaintiff transferred his share to Bazaler Rahman and became titleless. Sabina Khatoon by registered kabala dated 27th Falgun, 1339 BS corresponding to 11-3-1933 transferred his share to Joynal Abedin and become titleless. Anjunnessa as mother of Bazaler Rahman, lived in joint mess and having satisfied with the nurse of Bazaler Rahman, transferred her entire purchased land i.e. 3 and 5/8 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman at first week of January, 1935 orally and become titleless. As aforesaid, Bazaler Rahman become owner of 10 annas share, consisting of 18 and 1/8 decimals of land. Thereafter for ejmali land, Bazaler Rahman and Abul Hasim amicably partitioned and registered deed was executed on 24th Badra 1344 BS and registered on 10- 5-1937. In that partition deed Bazaler Rahman was settled with 10 annas and Abul Hasim was settled by 6 annas of land. While defendant in possession, Abul Hasim on 27th Badra, 1348 BS corresponding to 13-9-1941 executed and registered saf kabala deed transferring 2 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman. While Abul Hasim was in possession on remaining 8 and 7/8 decimals of land, by saf kabala deed dated 23-1-1942, transferred the suit land to Jabed Ullah and become titleless. In that deed it was mentioned 10.5 decimals of land but in fact, Jabed Ullah got possession for 81/8 decimals of land. Jabed Ullah on 28-4-1944 by saf kabala deed, transferred the said land to Bazaler Rahman and became titleless. In this way, Bazaler Rahman became owner of entire 29 decimals of land. MRR khatain was prepared for the aforesaid land in the name of Bazaler Rahman and recorded in MRR khatian No. 767 correctly and was published accordingly. The entire claim regarding suit land of plaintiff against this fact is totally false and without any basis. Bazaler Rahman to the very knowledge of his brother, sister and of entire locality, possesses the said land i.e. 29 decimals for more than 12 years and his title became perfect. Bazaler Rahman died leaving 4 sons, defendant Nos. 1-3 and Sukku Mea who inherited his land. The case of plaintiff that Bazaler Rahman died leaving 3 sons is totally false each sons of Bazaler Rahman got 7.25 decimals of land. Subsequently, Nasir Ahmed, defendant No.3, sold 1 decimal ofland to Majibullah by safkabala dated 1-2-1960. Again, this Majibullah by kabala dated 23-10-1961 transferred 1 decimal of land to Ali Ahmed. Momin Ullah through his father, as heir, got 7.25 decimals of land, having title and possession, by saf kabala dated 22-6-1959 transferred 1 decimals of land to Ahmed Ali. Momin Ullah and Nasir Ahmed, defendant No.2 and 3 on 21-5-1960 by safkabala deed transferred 13 decimals of land to Ali Ahmed and delivered possession and also become titleless. Taher Ahmed and Chukku Mea, another two sons, through their father, Bazaler Rahman, inherited 14.5 decimals of land, which they sold to Lutfunnessa by registered saf kabala dated 27-8-1960 and became title less. Ahmed Ali being owner and possessor of his purchased land, by deed of gift dated 24-7-1967 transferred the said land to Lutfunnessa and became titleless. Although in that deed of gift, it is written 26 decimals of land but in fact Lutfunnessa got more land legally as got by donor, Ahmed Ali. In this way, Lutfunnessa become owner of 29 decimals of land. Lutfunnessa on 16-11-1972 by two saf kabala deeds, transferred entire 29 decimals of land to HasinaAkter and AKM Mohammad Ullah, defendant No.5, who mutated their names in Mutation Case No. 1/1983-84 and 2/1983-84 and separated joma and opened khatian No. 2395 and 2396. It may be mentioned, against the purchase of Hasina Akhter, AKM Mohammadullah, Oaziullah and Monir and other as co-sharer of adjacent land, filed Miscellaneous Case No. 206 of 1980 and 245 of 1974 for pre-emption and both the cases were dismissed on 1-7-1980. Hasina Akhter and AKM Mohammadullah possessed the said land for more than 12 years with the knowledge of all and perfected their title. AKM Mohammadullah, while in possession, having title of 14.5 decimals of land by kabala dated 9-6-1990 transferred the said land to defendant Nos. 8,9 and 10 by exchange and delivered possession. Ahmed Ali also exchanged 14.5 decimals of land on 9-6-1990 with defendant No. 10 and become titleless. Defendant Nos. 8,9 and 10 after getting the land as aforesaid, by Mutation Case No. 97/90-91, mutated their names, opened khatian and payed rents regularly till now. In the suit land plaintiffs have no right, title and interest.

8. The further case of these defendants is that basic deed of plaintiff dated 17-4-1944 and Bazaler Rahman are false, fabricated without any consideration and not acted upon, null and void. Bazaler Rahman did not transfer 6 decimals of land on 17-4-1944 but Abdul Aziz Patwari claimed plaintiff and Bazaler Rahman did not exe- cute and register the said deed. In the deed dated 17-4-1944 signature, left thump impression and place of execution of Bazaler Rahman are all false, fabricated and manufactured and left thump impression is a totally false one. Abdul Aziz Patwari never got possession of any land. The deed dated 17-4-1944 was executed on false personaion in place of Bazaler Rahman. Bazaler Rahman if transferred 6 decimals of land to Abdul Aziz Patwari then in MRR survey along with Bazaler Rahman, name of his brother, Abdul Aziz Patwari ought to be recorded. The deed dated 17- 4-1944 was never acted upon. The entire statement regarding transfer of land from Bazaler Rahman and Abdul Aziz Patwari made in the plaint are totally false. Plaint case that Abdul Aziz Patwari got possession of 7.5 decimals ofland and Abdul Aziz Patwari died leaving son, Sirajul Islam and 3 daughters, Parul Begum, Minara Begum and Shamsunnahar as made in the plaint are entire false and those persons are imaginary and false person and they never was in possession of the suit land. Abdul Aziz Patwari was a title less and possessionless person and on this point plaintiff did not inherit anything and his heirs have no possession or title and purchase of the land by plaintiff by deed dated 29-11-1990 for 29 decimals of land do not confer any title as Abdul Aziz Patwari was titleless. Fatema Begum and Sirajul Islam did not have any right, title, interest and possession of purchase land and deed dated 29- 11-1990 is false, fabricated, not acted upon, with- out consideration and was manufactured for the purpose of the suit. Bazaler Rahman was titleless and, as such, from Arafatunnessa, Abdul Aziz Patwari and Hasina Akhter, daughter of Anwara Khatun did not get or inherit any land of Arafatunnessa, Entire plaint case is false and plaintiffs have no possession over the suit land. Defendant Nos. 8,9 and 10 after getting suit land as aforesaid and also on adjacent to the suit land constructed some pucca constructions, the suit having filed on false avertments is liable to be dismissed with costs.

9. This defendant in their additional written statement make out case that defendant Nos. 11- 12 are totally title less persons and plaintiffs purchased the said land from some title less and possessionless persons as such the statement of plaintiffs are totally false.

10. Defendant Nos. 11-12 did not file any appeal also this defendant did not move before this Court against the decision of the appellate court, as such, only for reference, the case may be considered.

11. The case of defendant-petitioner Nos.11-12 is that, Amzad Khalasi was the original owner of the suit land having right, and title. Arafatunnessa by saf kabala dated 25-12-1926 purchased 4 decimals of land from Amzad Khalasi. Amzad Khalasi having title and khas possession for remaining 25 decimals of land, died leaving son, Abul Hasim and 4 daughters, Solema Khatoon, Halima Khatoon, Chaiera Khatoon and Fatema Khatoon, sold 2 decimals ofland to Jabed Ullah by saf kabala dated 27-6-1932. Abul Hashem, son of, Amzad Khalasi, died leaving son, Abul Hashem, who inherited the property of Abul Hashem, sold 10.5 decimals of land to Jabed Ullah by kabala dated 23-1-1942. Bazaler Rahman purchased the said land from Jabed Ullah by saf kabala dated 28-4-1944. Bazaler Rahman by purchase and after the death of Arfatunnessa, as heir, become owner of the land left by Arfatunnessa and Jabed Ullah.Bazaler Rahman died leaving sons, Taher Ahmed alias Jalal Ahmed, Momin Ullah alias Chaku Miah, who inherited the property of Bazaler Rahman. Ali Ahmed purchased I decimal of land from Momin Ullah by kabala dated 26-2-1951. Ali Ahmed also purchased 1 decimal of land from added defendant No. 11; Kulsum Begum purchased 1 decimal of land from Ahmed Ali by kabala dated 6-7-1967. After purchase Kulsum Begum constructed tin shed house and also semi pucca house on the south-west corner of dag and possessing the same. Over the said 1 decimal of land, excepting defendant No. 11, no one has any title or possession. Defendant No. 11 on behalf of plaintiff and defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 and 12 looked after the property. Momin Ullah and Nasir Ahmed, son of Bazaler Rahman, after the death of Bazaler Rahman, having title over the property, by kabala dated 27-8-1960 sold some land to Ahmed Ali. Md. Ali Ahmed by deed of gift dated 24-5-1967 gifted the said land to his wife, Lutfunnessa. Anar Ullah purchased 3 decimals of land from Sayera Khatun, daughter of Amzad Khalasi, dated 9th Jaistha, 1375 BS. Against that deed, Ali Ahmed filed Miscellaneous Case No. 128 of 1969 in the court of Munsif, 1st Court, Laxmipur for pre- emption. While pre-emption case was in progress, Ali Ahmed died, leaving wife, Lutfunnessa and son, Nur Alam and daughter, Rahima Khatoon, who was substituted in his place, pre-emption case was dismissed on 4-7-1970 on compromise. Nur Alam and Nasima Begum having been owner and having khas possession of the suit land, by kabala deed No. 4556 dated 14-3-1987 transferred the property to plaintiff-petitioner. Defendant No. 12 after becoming owner on exchange, constructed two storied tin shed house, bamboo house and also constructed pucca house and since then, enjoying the land. The said 3 decimals of land which defendant No. 12 got by exchange is only living place of defendant No. 12. Defendant No. 12 has no other place to live. Defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 did not acquire any title or possession over the suit land. This defendant open holding No. 36 2(Kha) and regularly paying Municipal taxes. In some portion of the land of this defendant plaintiffs have no possession. The case of defendant No.8, 9 and 10 are totally false and they have no construction on the suit land and that in part of land of defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 there is caretaker and not acted upon and on the basis of deeds, defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 was never in possession. Defendant No. 9 as plaintiff filed Petition Case No. 409 of 1991 in the court of Upazilla Magistrate wherein an enquiry was held by the Upazilla Magistrate who found structures and possession of defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10. Defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 thereafter filed preemption case was which dismissed on 18-5-1992. Defendant No. 8 was the witness of the case. Plaintiff having not been made any prayer for partition, the suit is liable to be dismissed. If the plaintiff's case for partition is to be decreed, then these defendants are entitled for saham for (1+3) = 4 decimals of land and excepting this land, if plaintiffs' suit be decreed, then these defendants have no objection, with these avertments, defendants prayed for disposal of the suit.

12. Learned Subordinate Judge dismissed the suit and the learned Judge of appellate court decreed the suit.

13. Learned Assistant Judge while dismissing the suit holding inter alia that gift in favour of Bazaler Rahman by his mother Arafatunnessa in 1935 with deliver of possession has been proved by exhibits 2 (Chha) and admitted by defendant Nos. 8-10 and plaintiff; plaintiff also proved that Bazaler Rahman is the owner of 26.5 decimals of land which is also admitted; on consideration of exhibit (Ga) learned Judge found that there was mutual settlement about the land between Bazaler Rahman and Abul Hasim by partition deed dated 10-5-1937, where it was amicably settled that Bazaler Rahman will got 10 annas, Abul Hasim will get 6 annas which is also an admitted position; by registered kabala dated 28-4-1944 exhibit (Ga) to (Ga) 15, Bazaler Rahman purchased 6 annas share from Abul Hasim. Learned Judge also considered the deposition of PW 2, Ali Ahmed and held that it is admitted position that Bazaler Rahman become 16 annas title holder of suit khatian. Learned Judge also considered that at the time of MRR survey the other daughters and sons of Arafatunnessa were alive but they did not raise any objection against 16 annas ownership of the suit land in favour of Bazaler Rahman. Defendant Nos. 8,9 and 10, it is found by the learned Judge that by document, proved oral gift in favour of Bazaler Rahman which has been supported by exhibits 2(Cha) to 2(Jha) to Neo that plaintiffs purchased suit land from the successive heirs of Arafatunnessa. Thereafter, learned Judge discussed oral evidence of the witnesses and found that DWs 2, 3 and 4 proved Bazaler Rahman had 4 other brothers and one sister and also learned Judge considered the deposition of PWs 1 and 2 who admitted that the name of husband of Arafatunnessa and father of Bazaler Rahman was Ayub Ali, which is the case of defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10. Defendant No.9 as sharer, title holder, by exhibit 2 Chha, sold 6 decimals of land, which plaintiffs purchased from Anwara Khatun. Defendant Nos. 8, 9 and 10 claimed this deed as false, fabricated and not-binding upon, and in their depositions and written statements demand from plaintiffs to produce original deed but plaintiff did not produced and plaintiff did not give any explanation either orally or in the plaint as to why they did not produce this deed in evidence. Plaintiff also did not produce the deeds dated 7-6-1944 and 9-6-1944 in its original and it is also found by the learned Judge that by the deed dated 7-6-1944, and 9-6-1944, the predecessor of plaintiff exhausted his title of the exchange land and thereby from purchase from Anwara Khatun plaintiff did not acquire any title. Learned Judge also considered the depositions of the witnesses and found that neither PW 1 nor PWs 2 and 3 in their earlier depositions did properly describe the scheduled land and also found that PW 3 is the neighbor of the suit property. Learned Judge found witnesses of defendant Nos. 8-10 reliable. Learned Judge also found plaintiffs did not prove the PS khatian which was prepared wrongly and not created which has presumptive value. Learned Judge also found that plaintiff did not prove title of i.e. 4 sons and daughter of Amjad Khalasi and by deed plaintiff admitted PS Jorip. Learned Judge also found that plaintiff did not prove MRR khatian as wrongly recorded. Learned Judge also considered that plaintiff raised objection against Mutation Case and separated joma as a whole on 27-7-1983 but failed to prove that said recording was wrong and illegal and PW 1 did not state anything about their said mutation and separation of joma. Learned Judge also found that plaintiff although demanded but did not pay advelorem court fees as such the suit is not maintainable as per Order VII, rule 11 (c) read with section 149C of the Code of Civil Procedure. Learned Judge on consideration of depositions of witnesses ultimately held as:-

"তাহার কতেক নিঃস্বত্ববান ব্যক্তিগণের নিকট হইতে কতেক ভুয়া দলিলাত সৃজন করতঃ নাঃ বিবাদী ভূমিতে তাহাদের ভূয়া স্বত্বের দাবী করিয়াছে মাত্র। তাহা ছাড়া অত্র মোকাদ্দমায় বাদীপক্ষ তাহার কজ অব একশান প্রমান করিতে পারেন নাই। অধিকন্তু বাদী বন্টনের প্রার্থনা করিলেও কোন তারিখে বাদী শরিফ বিবাদিগনকে তলব তাগাদা করিয়াছেন তাহার বিন্দু মাত্রই তিনি আরজীতে উল্লেখ করেন নাই। তাহাছাড়া বাদী নালিশী ভূমির পি,এস,ও আর, আর, জরিপের বিষয় জানিয়া শুনিয়া কতেক দলিলাত সৃজনে ভূয়া স্বত্বের দাবী উখ্যাপনে অত্র মোকাদ্দমাটি দায়ের করিয়াছেন বলিয়া আমি মনে করি যে উপরোক্ত সুদীর্ঘ আলোচনার ভিত্তিতে-(৩)-(৫) বিচার্য্য বিষয়ের সিদ্ধান্ত বাদী পক্ষ ও ১১/১২ নং বিবাদিগনের প্রতিকূলে এবং ৮-১০ নং বিবাদীগণের অনুকুলে গৃহীত হইল।"

14. Plaintiff and Abdul Barek alias Manik Mea filed Title Appeal Nos. SO of 1997 and 21 of 1997. Both these appeals were heard analogously by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Laxmipur who by judgment and decree allowed both the appeals and decreed the suit. Learned Judge in the body of the judgment found that it is admitted fact that 29 decimals of land of District Survey Khatian No. 458, plot No. 3246 originally belonged to Amzad Khalasi. Learned Judge on consideration of exhibit 2-2(Ka) decided the share of Sabina Khatoon at 4 decimals of land. Learned Judge thereafter considered the case of defendant Nos. 8-10 that they claimed that Arfatunnessa orally gifted her 4 decimals of land to Bazaler Rahman but that oral gift was not at all proved. Learned Judge in support of such findings held that, principle of law that to prove gift, 3 essential ingredients must be proved, i.e. (i) there must have a declaration, (ii). acceptance of said declaration or offer and (iii) delivery of possession. It is settled principle of law that without delivery of possession no gift has been proved. Learned Judge found gift was executed in 1935 and Bazaler Rahman sold it by exhibit 2 Cha in 1944 but Bazaler Rahman did not make any respectful ground in exhibit 2 Cha that he got suit land by oral gift. Learned Judge also considered that bantaknama dated 10-5-1937 also did not mention in the recital of oral gift. Learned Judge considered that learned Judge of trial court committed gross illegality in not considering certified copy, exhibit 2 Cha dated 17-4-1944, in absence of original or in absence any explanation is in admissible, reversing that such finding of trial court as perverse as plaintiff stated that the said deed is aged about 50 years and the validity of said deed has not been challenged by Bazaler Rahman or his heirs as such at present, the validity of the deed cannot be questioned. Learned Assistant Judge took exhibit 2 Chha as illegal and on consideration exhibit 2 Cha dated 17-4-1944 learned Judge of the appellate court found that Abdul Aziz got 6 decimals of land and plaintiff purchased said 6 decimals of land from the heirs of Abdul Aziz, which plaintiff clearly proved and also proved possession of the plaintiff. Learned Judge also considered that defendant Nos. 8-10 claimed that Arafatunnessa had two other sons which had not been proved. Learned Judge thereafter found all the witnesses of plaintiff reside in and around of the suit land and witnesses of defendants are not adjacent to the suit land and people of suit property. Learned Judge also considered that Anwara Khatoon, daughter of Arafatunnessa, got 1 decimals of land through pre-emption case No. 147 of 1963 which was allowed on 8-6-1963, exhibit Chao. On these findings learned Judge found title of plaintiff and decreed the suit.

15. Learned Judge also found that plaintiff did not pay any court fees as required under Order VII, rule 11 (c) of the Code of Civil Procedure but the court fees can be submitted at any time.

16. Mr AKM Nazrul Islam, learned Advocate, appearing for the defendant, submits that, the defendant-respondent-petitioners are owner of the suit land measuring 14.5 decimals of land on the basis of deed of exchange from the rightful owners and they also claim separate saham in the suit land, since in a suit for partition the defendant having status of plaintiff and the plaintiff having  status of defendant vice versa and accordingly, when the trial court dismissed the suit, the appellate court cannot decree the suit for partition without ascertaining the respective share of the parties, the judgment and decree passed in the appeal is highly erroneous and bad in law and it is an error apparent on the face of the record occasioning failure of justice and, as such, the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court is liable to be set aside. Learned Advocate further submits that trial court found the plaintiff is out of possession of the suit property and also found that on the basis of the purchase he cannot get any share in the suit land measuring 10 decimals without any prayer for recovery of possession and partition without payment of advelorem court-fees is not maintainable and referred to the decision reported in 16 DLR 195 and the appellate court without ascertaining the share of the respective parties cannot pass the decree for partition and before realization of the advelorem court fees, the impugned decree is void ab-initio and, as such, cannot be given effect. Learned Advocate further submits that the appellate court hopelessly failed to consider genealogy of the transfer of the documents and illegally held that plaintiffs claim for partition is legal without ascertaining the title and possession of the plaintiff and in view of the fact that the trial court held that plaintiff has no title and possession and the suit is not maintainable without any prayer for khas possession on payment of advelorem court fees and, as such, the appellate court has not legally set aside the finding of facts arrived by the trial court.

17. Mr. Khair Ezaz Masood, learned Advocate, appeared for the opposite parties on both the rules, on the other hand, submits that, Abdul Aziz had one son, Serajul Islam and three daughters, Parul Begum, Minara Begum and Shamsunnahar and wife, Fatema Bibi and Amzad Khalasi had one son Abdul Haque, 4 daughters, Halima Khhatoon, Solema Khatoon, Chaiera Khatoon and wife, Fatema Khatoon who by exhibit 2 Kha dated 14-7-1930 transferred 14 decimals of land to Jabed Ullah. Abdul Huq, his son, sold 10 decimals of land to Jabed Ullah. The learned Judge of appellate court considered exhibit 2 (Kha) to 2 (Chha) and thereafter, passed judgment rightly and legally. Learned Advocate further submits that defendant Bazaler Rahman did not have 4 brothers and one sister and it is the case of plaintiff that Bazaler Rahman had 3 brothers and one sister which the learned Judge of appellate court having found, defendant could not prove, that Bazaler Rahman had 4 brothers legally justified in allowing appeal. Learned Advocate further submits that court of appeal below rightly held that exhibit 2 Chha, a basic deed dated 17-4-1944 is of certified copy but this deed being 30 years old has a legal foundation which confer title over the suit property: Plaintiff in order to prove their title produced in court certified copy of the deed dated 7-6-1944 and 9-6-1944 and this being deed for more than 30 years old has presumptive value. Learned Advocate further submits that appellate court in fact did not feel it necessary to find as to whether Bazaler Rahman had 4 brothers or 3 brothers as it is not necessary for deciding the suit.

18. On the submissions of the learned Advocates and on consideration of the plaint case with amendment, and case make out in written statements, depositions of the witnesses and exhibits filed by the parties, four questions calls for determination as (i) whether Arafatunnessa gifted 2 anna share orally to Bazaler Rahman in exclusion of other sharers legally, (ii)" whether exhibit 2 Cha to 2 Chha, deed dated 17-4-1944 and 9-6-1944 in absence of original deed can be said to be good deed of title and (iii) whether Bazaler Rahman had 4 brothers and one sister or 3 brothers and one sister (iv).whether the suit can be maintainable in absence of payment of advelorem court fee after demanded by court.

19. Mr. Khair Ezaz Masood, learned Advocate relied on the case of Abani Mohan Saha vs Assistant Custodian (SDO) Vested Property, Chand pur; 39 DLR (AD) 223 where it is held by the Appellate Division that "The plaintiff is claiming his title to the suit land on the basis of a deed of gift. I have got no doubt in my mind that the initial onus was on him to prove his title. The observation made in 32 DLR (AD) 29 would be of no avail to the appellant, as he failed to discharge his initial onus by proving his document of title. Had he succeeded to do so then the onus would have shifted on the enemy property authority to prove that the executants of the plaintiff's document, the sons of Surendra Mohan Saha, were residing in the enemy country at the relevant time," That means plaintiff is to prove his case.

20. Let us take first point at first i.e. whether oral gift is maintainable in law. DF Mulla defined hiba or gift is "a transfer of property, made immediately, and without any exhance," by one person to another, and accepted by or on behalf of the latter. It further been defined that "Every Mohammadan of sound mind and not a minor may dispose of his property by gift". Ingredience gift are (i) offer, (ii) acceptance and (iii) delivery of possession. Delivery of possession may either be actual or constructive. Mr Khair Ezaz Masood, learned Advocate, submits. that, of the three conditions there might be offer and acceptance but there is no sufficient evidence of taking physical possession. It may be true but at the same time it is seen that gift was between mother and son live in the same premises, in same mess. As per section 152(3) of Mulla's, Principles of Moharnmadan law when donor and donee both reside in same premises in that case. "No physical departure or formal entry is necessary in the case of immovable property in which the donor and the donee are both residing at the time of the gift. In such a case the gift may be completed by some overt act by the donor indicating a clear intention. on his part to transfer possession and to divest himself of all control over the subject of the gift. The principle for the determination of questions of this nature was thus stated by West, J., in the case of Sheikh Ibrahim vs Sheikh Suleman, 9 Born 146 followed by other Courts of the sub-continent that "When a person is present .on the premises proposed to be delivered to him, a declaration of the person previously possessed puts him into possession without any physical departure or formal entry." In the case of Abdul Sattar Ostragarvs Abu Bakkar Ostagar AIR 1977 Cal. 132 it is held that "When a father makes a gift of the dwelling house to his sons, and both the father and the donees (sons) are residing in the house, there is no need for delivery of possession." In the case of Ghulam Hassan vs Mumtaz Khan, 1956 PLD (WP) 1909 it is held that "In case of gift by father or guardian in favour of a minor, if a real and bonafide intention to make a gift is prove, law will be satisfied without a change of possession." In the case of Aurangzeb vs Daud Khan, PLD 195785 it is held that "No change of possession is necessary in the case of a gift by a grand-father to his minor grandson if the father is dead, for the grandfather is the person to take delivery on behalf of his grandson as his guardian." In the case of Natho vs Headyat Begum PLD 1952 Lahore 545 it is held that "It was entirely unnecessary for the mother to depart from the gifted premises in order to show the possession of the daughter, but, on the other hand, it was quite sufficient that it should be agreed between them that whereas previously the mother was the owner of the premises and the daughter was living with her, after the death, the daughter was the owner and mother was living with her." In the case of Zeenat Bibi vs Zaman Mehedi 1956 PLD 760 = 8 DLR 93 it is held that "It is unnecessary to point out that if the actual possession cannot be given by the donor to the donee, but the donor has done all that he could do to divest himself of the gifted property the gift would be considered to be complete and effective according to law."

21. Judicial decisions settled that when change of possession is unnecessary in the valid gift by a father to his minor child or by a guardian to his ward, all that is necessary is to establish a bonafide intention not more when donee lives in loco parentis with another, when donor and donee lived in the same house, subject of gift.

22. The authority opined that if gift is made to the donee who is not living with the donor or if the subject matter of the gift is in possession of a third party then delivery of possession is a must to be given in presence of witnesses. If it is challenged then it required to be proved as per law. But if gift is made in favour of donor's wife, or husband or daughter or son or ward who reside in the same house, such delivery of possession is not required, only evidence of the donor and donee is enough. Defendant's case is that Arafatunnessa orally gifted her entire share to Bazaler Rahman who is son as formal proof of delivery of possession is enough. In Gift propositor can exclude any one but in will or osiyatnama propositors has limitation. In gift donor could divest his entire property which immune from challenge. Court of appeal below did not consider the relationship in between donor and donee. It is admitted fact that Arafatunnessa lived with Bazaler Rahman in the same house in the same mess as such onus shifted upon the plaintiff, it also lies on plaintiff, to prove it otherwise but plaintiff did not adduce any such evidence. So, first question decided against plaintiff.

23. Now to the second point i.e. producing of certified copy of the title deeds by the plaintiff, exhibits 2 Cha to 2 Chha. Defendants challenge these deeds as false, fabricated, illegal and not acted upon. Section 65 of the Evidence Act permit to produce certified copy but for that, an explanation is required, certified copy is not photo copy. When the documents have been challenged as false, forged and fabricated, then, it is incumbent upon the plaintiff to produce the original. Naturally, when original document is lost, there is other method to prove it. Original is required to produce to find whether the signature and left thump impression appeared there in is of the person who executed the same. In certified copy, signature or left thump impression of the executants do not appear. In photo copy it does. Defendants in their written statement as well as in their depositions challenge the basic documents of title of plaintiff as false and for non production of originals but the plaintiffs goes to show the apprehension of defendants in respect of falsity of claim of the plaintiff on false document is true, legal and genuine.

<u>24. Mr. Khair Ezaz Masood, learned Advocate, on reference to the depositions, submits that PW 1 stated that he produced certified copy which is permissible in law but on a reading of the plaint or depositions of plaintiff we do not find any explanation as to why the originals have not been produced. Khair Ezaz Masood, learned Advocate further submits that executants as well as the scribe and witnesses died but there are other methods of proving the deeds, plaintiffs could call for the volume from Sub-Registry office. Certified copy of these two kabalas were produced and marked as exhibits 2 Cha to 2 Chha by the trial court. Learned Advocate submits that these documents being 30 years old has a presumptive value. Section 90 of the Evidence Act speak so, 30 years old document goes into evidence readily but the contents of it must prove to the hilt and that too, when the original produced, not certified copy.</u>

25. On consideration of entire matter, we are of the view that plaintiff did not take any proper step to discharge the onus and failed to prove the kabalas are not forged or in personation. It appears that plaintiff suppressed the documents from producing in court which infer a negative inference from court. Thus we are of the view that plaintiff cannot drive any benefit from exhibits 2 Cha to 2 Chha.

<u>26. When plaintiff instituted the suit it is desirable that plaintiff has all the arms under his belt to have a decree. It is also desirable that plaintiff 'shall' satisfy the court with fact, evidence of both kinds, oral or documentary for the decree prayed for. Weakness of defendant does not give decree to the plaintiff as it is not defendant who invoke the jurisdiction of court but is an invitee, his failure no way spoil plaintiff's claim. Plaintiff in all count must satisfy the court for the decree prayed for. A suit is decreed or dismissed at first on plaintiffs materials as such when we find plaintiff failed to make out a case for decree then naturally the suit would be dismissed.</u>

27. On the question of possession, it appears that trial court on consideration of a number of exhibits, held that plaintiff purchased the suit land from Ali Ahmed and Lutfunnessa but it appears that by this exhibit Ga series, title of Lutfunnessa has been extinguished, as such by purchase from titleless person plaintiff did not drive any title. On the question of possession the finding of trial court has not properly reversed by the appellate court but in cursory manner which is not lawful as such finding of the trial court stand.

<u>28. Above all, we find that trial court directed the plaintiffs to pay advelorem court fees, but plaintiff did not and without depositing advelorem court fees plaintiff filed the suit and also appeal. Learned Judge of the trial court could have dismissed the suit on this ground alone as under section 7 (lV)(c) of the Court fees Act unless court fees be paid even after demand by the court, suit cannot proceed. Plaintiff even in revisional stage and not even today, deposit the wanting court fees as such suit is barred under Order VII, rule 11(c) of the Code of Civil Procedure. We do not, either from order sheet of trial court or appellate court or High Court Division find plaintiff paid the advolerum court fees which is an added ground for dismissing the suit.</u>

29. We find substance in these two rules.

30. In the result, the rule of Civil Revision No. 1148 of 2001 and Civil Revision No. 4016 of 2009 are made absolute without any order as to costs.

31. The judgment and decree complained is set aside. Title Suit No. 56 of 1991 is dismissed.
